what: The test title `R-01 emails ab.c, a@b, @b.c, a@.c-less text a@bc and a@b@c.d each give an email error` is garbled and lists `a@.c` among the refused emails, while R-01's three conditions (one `@`, text on both sides, a dot after it) accept `a@.c` and ADR-007 says the rule is exactly R-01 and nothing stricter
why: a builder who reads the title as written writes a test that refuses what R-01 allows, and the tester's spec and the builder's test then disagree on the same input
fix: rewrite the title as `R-01 emails ab.c, a@b, @b.c, a@bc and a@b@c.d each give an email error` and, if `a@.c` is meant to be covered, add a separate title `R-01 email a@.c is valid because R-01 asks only for a dot after the @`

what: The test title `R-31 formatDate(2026-10-30, en-GB) gives 30 Oct 2026 in any time zone of the process` carries R-31, which is about personal data in errors, URLs and titles, not about date display
why: the trace will link R-31 to a date formatting test, so a reader of docs/TRACE.md gets a wrong picture of what proves R-31
fix: retag the title to `R-28 formatDate(2026-10-30, en-GB) gives 30 Oct 2026 in any time zone of the process` (R-28 is already in S8 Covers and names the date on the order view)

what: S3 puts `Intl.Collator` in `src/domain/customers.js` while ADR-003's module map gives `src/ui/format.js` `every Intl call`; the plan resolves the two accepted ADRs itself under Risks
why: a finder-contract reading ADR-003 alone can raise the domain Collator as a contradicted decision after the code is written, which costs a fix round
fix: add `D2. ADR-003 gives format.js every Intl call and ADR-007 sorts customers with Intl.Collator in the domain with the locale as an argument: confirm the domain Collator (recommended, ADR-003's own consequence line) in ADR-003 under ## Answered` to Decisions needed from the human

what: Step 3 bundles five concerns into one step of a six-file slice: the composition root, UI state, `commit`, the frozen code table, the global error listeners and the `hashchange` guard with the leave-a-form rule, and the guard is only proven in S11
why: a six-file slice whose central file is written blind, with its guard checked two slices later, is hard to review in one commit and hides where a defect in `main.js` came from
fix: either split S9 into S9a (index.html, styles.css tokens, main.js with commit and the listeners, screen 7.8) and S9b (components.js, screen 7.7, the hashchange guard) or add a manual check `- [ ] UX: leaving a form: ...` to S9 that is ticked once S11 is on screen, as S8 does for R-16

what: The S9 line `- [ ] R-21: with storage access denied in the browser, reload, the unavailable text shows with STO-02` checks the load-unavailable screen of ADR-004 and UI-SPEC 7.8, not R-21's words `If writing to localStorage fails ... the form stays open`
why: R-21 appears in S9 Covers on screen with a check that does not exercise a failed save, so the first real proof of `commit` keeping the form open is S11, and the trace for S9 overstates what was checked
fix: retag that line to `- [ ] R-20: with storage access denied ...` and drop R-21 from S9 Covers on screen, or keep R-21 and add `- [ ] R-21: with storage full, Start with empty data fails, the banner shows STO-02 and the screen stays`

what: S2 covers eight requirements across customers, orders and lines in one slice with fifteen tests; the plan says it stays one slice so `src/domain/validation.js` is not reopened three times
why: it is at the edge of the size rule and a failure in the line check blocks the commit of the customer check that is already green
fix: keep it, or split into S2 (customer and order checks, `R-01`, `R-02`, `R-06`, `R-07`, `R-17`, `R-31`) and S2b (line check, `R-11`, `R-12`) with the line `Reopens src/domain/validation.js to add the line check` on S2b

what: The test title `R-06 createOrder with no date input uses deps.today only as the form default, and an empty date gives the date error` names two behaviours, and the first (a form default) is not something a domain command can show
why: TS-02 asks one behaviour per test, and a builder cannot write an assertion for `used only as the form default` inside `createOrder`
fix: replace it with `R-06 createOrder with an empty date gives the date error and does not substitute deps.today`

what: The R-04 manual check names the order count and the no-legal-retention sentence but not the third part of R-04's message, that deleting those orders (R-08) and then the customer erases all of this customer's data
why: the human ticks the check without reading that sentence, so a banner missing it passes
fix: extend the line to `- [ ] R-04: on a customer with 3 orders, Delete customer shows no dialog, the banner names 3 orders, that no legal retention applies, and that deleting those orders and then the customer erases all of this customer's data; nothing changes`

what: Every Verify runs `npm test`, but ADR-001 says the human commits `package.json` before the first slice with no slice active, and the plan never states this precondition
why: S1's Verify fails on a fresh checkout until the human has made that commit, and the builder cannot add the file because no Files line lists it
fix: add one line to the plan header: `Before S1 the human commits package.json with the content of ADR-001, with no slice active; the plan lists it on no Files line.`

what: The Risks line says `shape.js has no test double for the browser's QuotaExceededError`, but the quota path lives in `createStorage` in `src/storage/storage.js`, not in `shape.js`
why: a builder reading the risk may look for the fake in the wrong file and the note misdescribes where the throw is caught
fix: change the Risks line to `storage.js has no browser QuotaExceededError under Node, so the fake throws a DOMException with that name`
